event.juno_heart2.4.text: Bram's mark is on every bar in here. Mine is thirty sketches under the coal bin. One of them is right. I haven't met it yet.
event.juno_heart2.4.why: the want gets a number and a hiding place; sharper thread

event.juno_heart5.3.text: I polished the flat until it showed my nose. Then my whole face. Then Bram behind me, nodding at it.
event.juno_heart5.3.why: the mirror catches Bram approving; subtext instead of a count

event.juno_heart5.2.text: Don't lose it! ...It's still Bram's pattern. Every line. The next one will be mine, once I find out what mine looks like.
event.juno_heart5.2.why: 'what mine looks like' names the real search, not just the next project

event.next_door.5.text: ...He said it. Out loud, with a witness. I need to sit on something official. The sign for next door is already drawn. It's under the coal, with everything else I'm not ready for.
event.next_door.5.why: ties the sign to the heart-2 hiding place; the true word lands last

event.juno_heart4.prank.text: Done! You're labeled! 'Guest (Excellent)'. I agonized over the parentheses. They're correct.
event.juno_heart4.prank.why: more specific pride; the joke lands on 'correct'

dlg.story.notes.juno.1.text: ...So. Now you know. Fifty-one notes, all me. Pencil, so anyone can pretend they don't know.
dlg.story.notes.juno.1.why: a count, and pencil becomes deniability: her shyness in one word

event.juno_heart10.intro.text: Hold out your hands. Both. I cut my own mark last night. A little anvil with a J hiding in it. You're first.
event.juno_heart10.intro.why: the mark gets a shape; 'You're first' says what the scene means

event.juno_heart10.give.text: First piece with my mark. A copper bar. {if quest:juno_gold=done}Copper on purpose: your gold went into the die. {/if}It weighs nothing. It's the heaviest thing I've ever handed anyone.
event.juno_heart10.give.why: weight against weight; gold branch kept intact

event.overheard_tilda_juno_1.l1.text: Tilda! Slate payment! Three clasps, one hinge, one smiley face. Stamped, not drawn.
event.overheard_tilda_juno_1.l1.why: cleaner list; 'stamped, not drawn' is craft pride in four words

adds.text: Bram taught me the hiss trick my first week. I screamed. Professionally.
adds.why: her first quench mirrors the player's; one Bram beat in a two-person scene

adds.text: Swing it once? Here, where I can see. ...There. That's the sound. That's the exact sound I drew.
adds.why: pays off her shipped 'I draw it first' line; the player's swing finishes the work

threads.juno_heart2: Thirty sketches of a maker's mark wait under the coal; which one is hers?
threads.juno_heart5: The sword is still Bram's pattern; she does not yet know what a Juno pattern looks like.
threads.next_door: The sign for the forge next door is drawn and hiding under the coal; the hook is still empty.
threads.story_notes_juno: Bram carries six notes in his apron and thinks they're from Tilda; Juno is letting him.
threads.juno_heart4: She's labeling the whole village next; the hall roof is first in line.
threads.juno_heart6: The crooked horseshoe stays hidden until 'the right day' to show Bram.
threads.juno_heart8: Bram hasn't put the horseshoe down, and the word she's waiting for is still unsaid.
threads.juno_heart10: Next door has an empty sign hook.
threads.juno_friend: Thursdays are swim day at the bucket; the player has a standing lane.
threads.juno_birthday: Your birthday answer now lives next to Click, the first clasp that ever closed.
threads.juno_courtship: Forty reasons exist on a list; only item one has been read aloud.
threads.juno_courtship2: The list grows by one patient item at a time until the player answers.
threads.juno_partners: The tiny anvil rings when tapped with a pin, and it will keep being tested on Bram.
threads.overheard_piper_juno_1: The anvil has a fan; Piper's teeth are owed a quieter song.
threads.overheard_piper_juno_2: 'Song (Forge)' will be hammered at the smithy all week; listen for it.
threads.overheard_piper_juno_3: Front row at the crate stage is Juno's; she means to hammer and watch at once.
threads.overheard_tilda_juno_2: The flour sack has waited by the hook jar for years; Juno's slate now says 'Owed (Forever)'.

notes: I can carry the Edmund seed (the tiny brass key I made for 'a box he'd lost the lock to'), but none of my scenes could take it without doubling threads; suggest a daily-talk or letter slot for it.
juno_heart10 now gives the mark a shape: a little anvil with a J in it. If Bram's lines or the next_door sign art describe her mark, align to that.
The juno.courtship dialogue graph is shared by both courtship scenes, so its lines stay generic enough to fit either ask; the scene-specific intros and afters carry the difference.
Kept dlg.juno.birthday.0 identical to the shipped line on purpose; most of hearts 4, 6 and 8 survive because they already land, and polishing would only loosen them.
